observation.source_interface: MNCS Environment pytest, Python compileall, and Git diff checks

verified_behaviors: Procfs process I/O reads are byte-bounded and missing or partial measurements remain explicit.
CPU ticks, RSS boundary samples, RSS high-water growth, and process I/O deltas are derived only when the same process birth identity brackets the interval.
Recovery-scan owner rows link resource deltas to the exact service execution identity, and the path-free trace projection retains those deltas.
The ECI owner summary retains at most one resource record per owner and reports total and omitted record counts.
The ECI keeps ambient fulfillment not-established and continues to read previous owner-summary schema versions.
The live resource CLI test exercises actual procfs counters without opening Store.

observation.scope_limit: The repository-wide suite was not run; 21 cases requiring the external compiler or Automation checkout were skipped.

pressure_hypothesis.title: Ambient owner executions lack bounded process-resource evidence
pressure_hypothesis.subsystem: MNCS Environment resource observation, coherence scheduling, and ECI
pressure_hypothesis.basis: An earlier resident process sample recorded high I/O and memory use but ended before a trace was available, while current owner-pass projections correlated execution IDs and elapsed time without process counters.
pressure_hypothesis.actionable_recommendation: Sample the scheduler process around existing owner runners, link deltas to exact service execution IDs, retain a bounded ECI view, and make process and child-process attribution limits explicit.

measurement_limits: Scheduler-process counters exclude spawned children and can include work in the bracketed interval not caused by the owner service.
The projection relationship is verified with deterministic fixture evidence; this session did not run a fresh resident tick or observe a live per-owner resource delta.
Verification proves the evidence path and bounded parsing, not reduced agent burden, service fulfillment, or improved runtime cost.
